title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide (2026)
author: Samantha Liu
content:
Summary
-------
This guide consolidates Redwood Inference's people operations best practices for hiring, candidate evaluation, employee onboarding (0-90 days), and the performance & feedback cycle for managers. It provides standardized, auditable processes, reusable templates, and owner/RACI guidance so teams deliver a consistent candidate and employee experience while maintaining legal/compliance guardrails.

Intended audience
-----------------
- People Ops partners
- Hiring managers
- Interviewers and interview loop coordinators
- New hires and onboarding buddies
- People managers conducting performance reviews

Key objectives
--------------
1. Reduce time-to-offer while maintaining hiring quality and EEO compliance.
2. Provide a repeatable 30/60/90 onboarding blueprint aligned to role families.
3. Standardize the performance/feedback cycle (annual review + continuous feedback).
4. Equip managers with templates, timelines, and escalation steps.

1) Hiring process overview
--------------------------
Owner: people-ops (partnering with hiring manager)

High-level steps (typical engineering hire)
1. Requisition creation & approval
   - Hiring manager submits req in Greenhouse with role profile, level, justification, and compensation band.
   - People Ops reviews for budget, headcount, and EEO language within 3 business days.
2. Sourcing & screening
   - Recruiter sources via internal referrals, job boards, and partners.
   - Initial recruiter screen: 30 minutes to confirm interest and basic fit (availability, salary expectations, visa status, location).
3. Interview loop design
   - Standard loop: Recruiter screen -> Manager screen -> Two technical interviews (coding/architecture or system-design for senior roles) -> Cross-functional interview (product/PM/design as relevant) -> Team/culture interview -> Final manager interview.
   - Each interviewer gets a scorecard and a documented evaluation rubric.
4. Calibration & debrief
   - Hiring debrief within 24 hours of final interview. Recruiter schedules, collects scorecards, and documents consensus.
   - If consensus unclear, hiring manager escalates to People Ops for calibration with a peer manager.
5. Offer & negotiation
   - Compensation package prepared by recruiter with People Ops approval.
   - Standard timeline: offer extended within 3 business days post-decision.
6. Background & reference checks
   - Initiated upon verbal offer acceptance; completed prior to start date.

Interviewer expectations & hygiene
---------------------------------
- Be on time, share the interview rubric with the candidate, and provide clear pass/fail signals.
- Use the standardized scorecard (see template below) and submit immediately after the interview.
- Avoid asking off-limits questions (age, marital status, medical, etc.) - see Legal FAQ in security-and-compliance.

Interviewer scorecard template (use as Greenhouse/Confluence form)
- Role: [string]
- Interviewer: [name]
- Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Core competencies evaluated (each 1-5): Technical skills, Problem solving, Communication, Ownership, Team fit
- Overall recommendation: Strong Hire | Hire | No Hire
- Notes (concrete examples, red flags)

Diversity & fairness checkpoints
--------------------------------
- At least one diverse slate goal for every open role when feasible.
- Interview panel should include members with varied perspectives.
- People Ops will conduct blind résumé options for roles where bias risk is high.

2) Offer & preboarding
----------------------
Offer components
- Base salary, equity grant (if applicable), target bonus/commission, start date, relocation/remote stipend, benefits highlights.
- People Ops owner signs off on total comp against band and internal equity.

Preboarding checklist (to be completed between offer acceptance and start date)
- Send welcome email with start logistics, first-week agenda, IT forms, and manager welcome note.
- Create user accounts and licenses (Slack, Google, Jira, GitHub, Redwood Console staging access as relevant).
- Assign an onboarding buddy and schedule 1:1s for week 1.
- Share 30/60/90 plan template tailored by role.

3) Onboarding: 0-90 day plan
---------------------------
Owner: hiring manager (execution) with People Ops support

Purpose: Ramp new hires quickly to meaningful contribution while connecting them to team norms and company culture.

Common 30/60/90 milestones (engineer example)
- Day 0-7 (Orientation & setup): Accounts provisioned, security training complete, meet team, first small contributor task (setup or docs).
- Day 8-30 (Learning & first delivery): Complete codebase walk-through, own a minor bug/feature, attend triage and standups, 1:1 weekly with manager.
- Day 31-60 (Ownership & impact): Lead a small feature or significant bugfix, present learnings to team, start cross-team collaboration.
- Day 61-90 (Autonomy & roadmap alignment): Deliver end-to-end feature or owning a production metric, propose improvement(s) to process or product.

Buddy responsibilities
- Be the day-to-day go-to for onboarding questions for the first 90 days.
- Schedule shadow sessions for team rituals (on-call, releases, retros).
- Provide continuous feedback to manager on ramp progress weekly for first month, then biweekly to 90 days.

Manager checklist (first 90 days)
1. Day 0: Welcome message, first-week calendar, and expectations.
2. Week 1: 1:1 to set priorities, review 30/60/90, confirm environment access.
3. End of month 1: Written check-in (manager to employee) summarizing progress and open items.
4. 45-day quick calibration with People Ops if ramp is delayed or there are signals of misfit.
5. 90-day formal check-in and decision on continued employment (for probationary hires where applicable).

4) Performance & feedback cycle
--------------------------------
Rhythm and timeline
- Continuous feedback: encouraged year-round (real-time recognition and improvement notes in Lattice).
- Quarterly check-ins: brief manager/employee set to align goals (optional cadence per team).
- Annual performance cycle: goal-setting in Q4 for next year; reviews conducted in Q1.

Performance review workflow
1. Self-review (employee) - due 2 weeks before manager review window.
2. Manager review & calibration - manager drafts review and collects peer feedback.
3. Calibration: People Ops facilitates cross-team calibration panels to ensure consistency across levels and bands.
4. Calibration outcome: rating and development plan finalized.
5. Review meeting: manager discusses review, rating, and development plan with employee.

Rating philosophy
- Focus on evidence-based examples and outcomes (metrics, shipped work, cross-team impact).
- Avoid using single-event judgments; use trend data across the review period.

Promotion & leveling guidance
- Promotions require demonstrated sustained impact against the target level rubric and at least two strong peer manager endorsements.
- Compensation adjustments tied to performance outcomes and market adjustments; People Ops owns approval.

5) Feedback, coaching, and performance improvement
--------------------------------------------------
Informal coaching
- Encourage managers to document coaching conversations and short action items in Lattice or manager notes.

Formal performance improvement plan (PIP)
- Triggered when documented coaching for 60+ days shows insufficient improvement.
- Manager drafts PIP with People Ops within 5 business days of escalation and defines measurable objectives, timeline (typically 30-90 days), success criteria, and check-in cadence.
- People Ops reviews legal risks and maintains records.

Exit and offboarding
--------------------
- See separate offboarding checklist (link) for IT de-provisioning, exit interview, and knowledge transfer. Manager must complete offboarding within 3 business days of notice.

6) Manager responsibilities & good practices
-------------------------------------------
- Set clear expectations at hire and during 1:1s. Document goals and milestones.
- Provide regular, timely feedback (both praise and areas for growth).
- Run structured 1:1s with an agenda; track action items.
- Escalate people issues to People Ops early (within 48 hours of concern).
- Ensure career conversations at least twice per year and document outcomes.

7) Templates & sample language
------------------------------
Offer acceptance email (short)
"Hi [Name], welcome to Redwood — we’re excited to have you. Your start date is [date]. Please complete the attached new hire forms. Your manager, [Manager], will reach out with your first-week plan. If you have any questions, reply to this thread or reach out to people-ops@redwood.com."

30/60/90 template (manager to customize)
- Focus areas: Technical ramp, product/context knowledge, team processes, and initial goals.
- Success measures: Deliverable(s), knowledge checks, and stakeholder feedback.

Manager feedback script (for difficult conversations)
1. State the observation and desired outcome.
2. Cite specific examples and impact.
3. Ask for the employee’s perspective.
4. Agree on next steps and timeline.

8) Compliance & recordkeeping
-----------------------------
- People Ops stores offer letters, background checks, and review artifacts in the HRIS (Workday) / secure People Ops drive.
- Retention policies follow legal and privacy requirements - refer to security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention.

9) Escalation & who to contact
-------------------------------
- Hiring process delays or disputes: people-ops@redwood.com
- Legal or compliance questions about hiring: legal@redwood.com
- Manager coaching escalation: your People Ops business partner
